record.paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity
record.original_question: Does there exist an exact purely radiative vacuum Einstein spacetime with complete smooth future and past null infinity, regular timelike infinities, and positive mass?

evidence.quote: Give an exact "purely radiative spacetime", i.e. a solution to the Einstein vacuum equations which has complete smooth ~±, regular i±, and positive mass, or show the existence of such a spacetime.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Construct, or prove the existence of, a smooth Lorentzian 4-manifold $(M,g)$ satisfying the vacuum Einstein equations $\mathrm{Ric}(g)=0$ with the following properties:

1. (Purely radiative / asymptotic completeness.) $(M,g)$ admits a conformal compactification in the sense of Penrose with smooth, complete future null infinity $\mathscr{I}^+$ and smooth, complete past null infinity $\mathscr{I}^-$.

2. (Regular timelike infinities.) The conformal compactification possesses regular future and past timelike infinity points $i^+$ and $i^-$, at which the unphysical metric and the conformal factor extend smoothly (so that, in particular, $\mathscr{I}^+$ is the future light cone of $i^-$ … no, rather, $\mathscr{I}^\pm$ are generated by complete null geodesics emanating from $i^\mp$ in the conformal completion, and the conformal structure is smooth at $i^\pm$).

3. (Positive mass.) The ADM (equivalently, Bondi) mass of $(M,g)$ is strictly positive.

The problem is to exhibit such a spacetime explicitly, or to prove abstractly that at least one such spacetime exists. (Minkowski space satisfies (1) and (2) but has zero mass; the Schwarzschild and Kerr solutions have positive mass but fail to have complete smooth $\mathscr{I}^\pm$ together with regular $i^\pm$.)
artifact.category_tag: General relativity / asymptotic structure of vacuum spacetimes
artifact.status_search_result: No explicit example of a vacuum Einstein spacetime simultaneously having complete smooth past and future null infinity, regular timelike infinities $i^\pm$, and positive mass is known. Friedrich's work on purely radiative spacetimes (Comm. Math. Phys.) and subsequent literature on conformal completions provide frameworks and partial existence results in terms of free data at $i^-$, but no concrete positive-mass example with all the stated regularity has been produced; the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: On purely radiative space-times
status_evidence.snippet: Purely radiative spacetimes are solutions of Einstein's vacuum field equations with smooth structure at past null infinity forming the future null cone at past timelike infinity with complete generators.
status_evidence.claim: Framework for purely radiative vacuum spacetimes; existence with positive mass not established.

status_evidence.title: On static and radiative space-times
status_evidence.snippet: To any static solution exists a certain 'radiative solution' which has a smooth structure at past null infinity and is regular at past timelike infinity.
status_evidence.claim: Related construction yields regularity at one timelike infinity, but full bi-regular positive-mass example not produced.

status_evidence.title: Conformal Infinity (Living Reviews in Relativity)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of conformal completions; existence of vacuum spacetimes with complete smooth scri and regular i± is a long-standing problem.
status_evidence.claim: Survey indicates the existence question for such purely radiative spacetimes with positive mass is open.
